decisions.reason: Cryptoassets and FX markets are distinct topics; sharing cross-border movement or complexity does not form a direct review relationship.
CH41 provides the concrete framework for regulatory reporting obligations; CH49 expands on a specific deficiency (defensive SARs) within that reporting system.
CH41 defines the KYC/CDD control framework at onboarding; CH54 operationalizes and expands this framework specifically through electronic KYC benefits.
Blockchain benefits and explorer reliability are related to blockchain technology but do not share a summary, illustration, grounding, or contrast relationship.
Both CPs list financial crime threats and predicate crimes but are parallel sector-specific vs. general lists; neither grounds, summarizes, nor illustrates the other.
Data cleansing methods and automated batch screening are distinct operational processes; sharing the concept of batch processing does not establish a grounds relation.
OECD Anti-Bribery Convention and G20 ACWG strategies are parallel international frameworks; one does not ground, summarize, or illustrate the other.
Hong Kong AI ethics guidelines and financial sector ML vulnerability are unrelated topics; no valid cross-chapter relation exists.
CH58 provides the concrete definition and framework of data taxonomy; CH47 applies this structure in the process of classifying and transforming collected data into intelligence.
Both are case studies demonstrating different legal frameworks and partnerships; they are parallel examples and do not illustrate, summarize, or ground each other.
